title: Spelling mode
goal: Know how a word with no pronunciation on record is written letter by letter, and how a spelled run is read back.

blocks.x: A few words have no pronunciation on record anywhere (`aboveground` is not in CMUdict, MFA's dictionary or WikiPron), so there are no sounds to run the onset, vowel and coda tables against. Spelling mode writes such a word with **every letter struck explicitly**, one stroke per letter.

Most of CMUdict's gaps never reach spelling mode: `src/ipa.rs` translates MFA's, then WikiPron's, IPA pronunciation into the ARPAbet CMUdict uses and fills it in before the rules see the word (see [a stroke, and the setup](#/ref/how-stroke-setup)). Neither source marks lexical stress, so a translated word's stress is a first-syllable-primary guess. Spelling mode is for what is left after that.

items: A spelling-mode run starts with `~` instead of `+`. `~` is a second virtual bit in the stroke (the 25th), next to [the join key](#/ref/join-key)'s 24th.
It means: read this stroke, and every following stroke that carries the ordinary join key, as a letter chord, not as sounds.
Only the first stroke carries `~`. The rest are ordinary continuations, `+` included.

blocks.x: `rules/spelling.toml` gives each letter exactly one bare chord, with no `-LGTS` ender: the `~`/`+` marker already says the run is spelled, so there is nothing to confuse it with. The chords are the primary ones from the [fingerspelling alphabet](#/ref/fingerspelling/the-alphabet); the second "magnum" chords (`AOEU` for *i*, `SKWRAEU` for *j*, `STKPWHR` for *z*) are not used here.
*y* is `KWH` here, not the `KWR*` of the glued letters.

items: `Rules::resolve` checks the first stroke for the spell bit before anything else.

If it is set, the outline goes to `Rules::resolve_spelling`: it strips `~` from the first stroke and `+` from each stroke after it, looks each bare chord up in the letter table, and concatenates the letters in order.
There is nothing to disambiguate: no vowel-key collision, no ranking of sounds, because each letter was struck, not inferred.

blocks.x: `Rules::spell_word(word)` is the exact inverse: it looks each letter up in the table and returns the outline with `~` on the first stroke and `+` on every one after it. It returns nothing for a word with a character outside plain a-z. `lookup`, `!explain` and `!quote` fall back to it once a word has no pronunciation, rather than calling the word untypeable.

`cargo run -- plugin` generates the same letter table and dispatch into the deployed WASM plugin, as it does for the phonetic tables (see [the fallback](#/ref/fallback/keeping-the-plugin-honest)). There is no second hand-kept copy.
Not yet on a physical key

`~` has no physical key in the live keymux config yet. Spelling mode works through `cargo run -- resolve` and the generated plugin, but you cannot strike it at a keyboard today. Until then, spell a word with the glued fingerspelling letters (`A*`, `PW*`, ...; see [Fingerspelling](#/ref/fingerspelling/fingerspelling-in-running-text)).
